develop.dumpsText: The database dumps will be useful if you need to process a lot of data quickly — in cases where the web service is not able to respond quickly enough. The latest database dump can be found <dumpLink>at this address</dumpLink>. A dump is made every week.
develop.heading: Developing with BookBrainz
develop.lead: We aim to make it as easy as possible to use the data stored in BookBrainz. If you’re a developer wanting to make programs that depend on BookBrainz, we have a web service available, and are releasing database dumps regularly.
develop.sourceText: BookBrainz runs on open source software. If you wish to access the source and contribute to the project, please see <githubLink>our github page</githubLink>.
develop.webServiceText: The web service is the primary way of getting BookBrainz data. The key advantage of using the web service over the dumps is that you don’t need to install any database engine — you can access the data through the internet. The web service is currently in alpha version and a <docsLink>live documentation is served at this address</docsLink>.

Although there was an initial burst of activity and good progress made on the site design, after a month or so, Sean didn't have time to maintain the initial level of activity.
about.storyPart3Mid: , started to take an interest in the project. New discussions were held in the BookBrainz IRC channel, and progress was made on a new node.js site and webservice. Recently, in order to reduce duplication of code, it was decided to once again use node.js for all code, and work is ongoing to achieve this.

q1._self: How do I add a book?
q1.a1: First and foremost, search for both the author and the title of the book to avoid creating duplicates.
q1.a2: If a Work and an Edition containing it exist, the questions below will help you decide whether to create a new Edition.
q1.a3: Otherwise, here is a step-by-step procedure:
q1.step2Post: Work with a relationship to the Author
q1.step2Pre: On the Author page, click on 'Add Work' to create a
q1.step3Mid: Edition with a relationship to the Work.
q1.step3Pre: On the Work page, click 'Add Edition' to create an
q1.step3Sub1Post: Edition Group will be created automatically, but you can select an existing one
q1.step3Sub2Post: Publisher if you cannot find an existing one
q1.step4: To enter another format of the same book (see explanations below), go to the Edition Group and click the 'Add Edition' button. Repeat step 4.

q2._self: When should I create a new Edition of a Work?
q2.item1: When it is published in a different format (e.g. paperback and e-book)
q2.item2: When there are substantial content (textual or editorial) changes
q2.item3: Translations will both be a new Work and a new Edition for it.
q2.item4: Add a relationship between the original and the translated Works
q2.item5: New cover or changed credits/attribution on the cover

q3._self: When should I not create a new Edition of a Work?
q3.item1: Minimal changes as in proofreading errors
q3.item3: Reprints of the same Edition. You can mention “Reprint – [date]” in the annotations.
q3.item4: When the edition uses the same ISBN (with rare exceptions)

q4._self: When should two Editions be part of the same Edition Group?
q4.introPre: Edition Groups exist to group together all the variations of an edition (an identifiable set of works) in a given language. Here are examples of Editions that should be part of the same Edition Group:
q4.item1: Different formats of the same edition (paperback, hardcover and e-book by the same publisher)
q4.item5: Co-editions (same book published in different countries by different publishers)

help.glossaryIntro: Here is a short description of some of the main terms you will encounter. Some terms are borrowed from MusicBrainz; click on the term to be redirected to the MusicBrainz guidelines or a definition.
help.glossaryPrintingDescPost: One edition of a work may have any number of printings, e. g. a same Edition can have a first impression and a second impression.
help.glossaryPrintingDescPre: – A batch of identical copies of an edition of a work that is printed in a same, single production set-up.
